name: Twitch
tagline: Live video streaming platform with chat, subscriptions, and a creator payout economy.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The technical part of Twitch is genuinely a weekend project: RTMP ingest, HLS transcode, a WebSocket chat room, done. None of that is what Twitch sells. What it sells is millions of concurrent viewers who show up because other viewers are there, a discovery surface that sends strangers to your channel, and a payments and payout system that moves subscription money to creators in dozens of countries. A personal stream server gives you a URL you text to friends, which is a fine thing to own and a completely different product. If you want an audience, you cannot build one in an empty folder.
coreLoopDIY: Self-hosted RTMP ingest from OBS, transcoded to HLS, played back in a browser page with a live chat sidebar.
requirements: A VPS with real upload bandwidth, or a home box plus port forwarding
OBS or similar on the streaming machine
A domain and TLS cert if you want it to work outside your LAN
Significant egress budget if more than a handful of people watch
whatYouLose: Discovery: nobody finds your stream unless you personally send them the link
Subscriptions, bits, ads, and the payout plumbing that turns viewers into income
Global CDN edge delivery, so viewer count is capped by your server's uplink
Mobile apps, clips, VOD archiving, raids, emotes, mod tools, and the moderation stack
Scale resilience: a surprise 500 viewers takes the box down instead of being a good day
moatNotes: Two-sided: creators go where viewers are, viewers go where creators are, and the payout rails make leaving expensive for anyone earning real money.
whyPeopleStillPay: Viewers pay for Turbo and subscriptions because the money goes to a specific person they want to support, which is a social act and not a feature you can self-host. Creators stay because the platform delivers an audience they did not have to acquire, handles payments in currencies they have never heard of, and absorbs the bandwidth cost of a stream going unexpectedly viral. A personal server inverts every one of those: you pay the egress, you recruit the audience, you invoice nobody. The streaming tech has been commodity for a decade; the reason that fact never dented Twitch is that the tech was never the product.
notes: The stream server is a weekend; the audience is not. The moat is two-sided network effects plus the payout rails that make a successful creator unable to afford to leave.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted live streaming server for one person streaming to a handful of friends. Stack: docker compose, MediaMTX for RTMP ingest and HLS output, a small Node 20 + Express server for the web page and chat, hls.js for playback, plain HTML and CSS, no framework, no build step.

In scope:
- docker-compose.yml with two services: mediamtx (RTMP in on 1935, HLS out on 8888) and web (the Express app on 3000).
- MediaMTX configured for one stream path named 'live', protected by a publish key read from STREAM_KEY in .env. Low-latency HLS on, 2 second segments.
- A single page at / with a video element playing the HLS url via hls.js, an offline placeholder when the stream is down, a live viewer count, and a chat panel on the right.
- Chat over a WebSocket on the Express server using the 'ws' package. Users pick a display name on join, stored in localStorage. Keep the last 100 messages in memory and replay them to new joiners. No database, no accounts, no persistence across restarts.
- Rate limit chat to 1 message per second per connection and cap messages at 300 characters. Escape all user input before rendering.
- A /health endpoint returning whether MediaMTX currently has a publisher on the 'live' path, polled from its API.
- An optional ROOM_PASSWORD in .env: if set, the page requires it before connecting to chat or loading the video.
- README with the exact OBS settings to paste: server url, stream key, recommended bitrate, and a warning that each viewer costs you real upload bandwidth.

Out of scope, do not build: VOD recording, clips, user accounts, payments, subscriptions, emotes, moderation tools, mobile apps, multi-channel support, transcoding ladders, any CDN integration, any analytics or telemetry.

All secrets in .env with a committed .env.example. Everything must run with 'docker compose up' and nothing else.
